title: [PC] CHROMEDRIFT – cyberpunk roguelike deckbuilder where you fight in the flesh and in the net at once
author: StitchworkGames
selftext:
Hi! I'm a solo developer and I'm looking for people to break the alpha of my deckbuilder.

**What it is**  
  
CHROMEDRIFT is a roguelike deckbuilder in the vein of Slay the Spire, set in Neo-Kessel, a vertical megacity built on a drowned one. You play Kira, a runner from the flooded lower city, climbing through three acts to reach ARGUS, the AI that runs the place.  


**What is different**

\- **Two layers, one fight.** Every enemy has a body (HP) and a firewall (ICE). Guns and fists hit the Flesh, hacks hit the Net. Break an enemy's ICE and it is compromised: it skips its next move and takes 50 % more damage. Some enemies have no net at all, some are nothing but net.  
\- **Body versus machine.** Implants go into real body slots (eyes, arms, neural port, nerves, skin) and each one costs Humanity. Your Humanity puts you in one of three zones: Human, Hybrid or Machine. Cards carry Instinct lines that only work while you are human and Protocol lines that only work once you are not. Both paths are strong, neither is free, and the story and the endings react to what you became.  
\- **Heat.** The strongest cards overheat your chrome. Push it and hit harder, or cool down and live through the next turn.  
\- **Nothing hidden.** Every enemy shows its next move. Pick a card, point at a target, and the game shows the result before you commit ("21 → 15 (−6)"). A forecast tells you what the end of the turn will cost you.  


**The look**  
  
Late-80s and early-90s cel anime: flat cels over painted backgrounds, hard two-tone shadows, a lot of black, one scene color per act (rust and yellow, clinical white and teal, black and green). Screens are laid out like manga pages. Animation is deliberately limited: figures hold a pose and snap to the next one, hits get an impact frame, and the picture stops for a moment when you get hurt. Rain and still water rather than neon everywhere.  


**What I would love to hear**  
  
\- Where did your run end, and what killed you?  
\- When did Flesh and Net click, or did it never?  
\- Did you install implants? Did Humanity matter to you?  
\- Any moment where you did not know what to do or why something happened  
\- Bugs, typos, bad translations

**Please message me for a** [**itch.io**](http://itch.io) **download link if you are interested.**

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
DM sent. 

...You should probably just link to the demo if you have it. Asking people to DM you is an extra layer of friction that will cause a lot of possible testers to pass on trying it.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/1fon1islw3vh1.png?width=1891&format=png&auto=webp&s=d93a472f99777837bfe5bf04ebd74c8aa73eaf92

  
This game has the potential to be something extremely special.

  
So, some stuff to get out of the way first: 

 \- I am extremely impressed with the presentation. The soundscape, the music scoring, the UI, the layout, the intentionality / ergonomics of where everything is placed; it feels great. The little bits of movement and animation everywhere make things feel alive. It's just great. Each act also has its own clear identity.  
  
 \- ...While the presentation is great, the AI art is... VERY AI. I almost hesitate to critique it because it is such an artifact of this era, it would almost be a shame to see it go. It doesn't look, per se, bad... and particularly here, in a package that could be well made, it almost feels like an act of preservation to keep it. It doesn't feel very placeholder-y. 

...But it does let the presentation down, a lot. Quite a few pieces I had to ask, 'is this really the best generation the developer could find, or is this all just placeholder so they really didn't care about how it looked?' 

 \- The writing, likewise, is SO very AI. And unlike the art, it's not worth preserving. There's no charm to it and it robs the game of a sense of place. The character designs were quite interesting, but they had no voice because the AI doesn't know how to talk.

 \- There's quite a bit of technical roughness to the game that I'm not going to focus on as part of the critique because it's safe to assume these are the sort of things that will be polished. But yeah... the interface fights the player in the upgrade screen, sometimes the text in the pre-fight screen just randomly shrinks, the resolution doesn't quite feel right in the fights and there's an unresponsiveness to the continue buttons in the Street scenes, to name a few things.

  
With that out of the way: 

What YOU have put into this is SO GOOD. And I totally get that Slay the Spire is a great foundation to build on, but seriously, you don't need it. If this were my project, I would go through all of the cards that are StS analogues and just completely rework them (or at least heavily consider what they are doing here). The Humanity Vs Machine system is excellent, as is the decision to create 2 distinct damage types that actually lean into some very distinct styles of play. I don't think the game currently trusts enough of that foundation; I think it needs to go even further in that direction. 

I think runs also need to be just shorter overall. Fight length / time to kill felt approximately right, but the run itself felt like it was dragging a bit - IMHO there are just a hair too many nodes for each act. I'd shave off 2-3 nodes from each and see how it feels after. I like the decision to not have a map and instead just provide the player with an easy binary choice, but sometimes this leads to non-choices; like, do I want a fight after this one + black market, or... just a fight? There's no reason to pick the first option. So that might be a thing to look into, making sure the choices are always a bit more balanced that that.

Enemy design and variety is fantastic. I have no notes; every turn felt like a meaningful interaction.

Thank you for not deciding to just throw a random hacking minigame into the game because cyberpunk. God I hate hacking minigames. 

  
Great work! 

I wish you good luck with this.

replies.author: StitchworkGames
replies.body: Thank you very much for your comprehensive and detailed feedback. I definitely will look into the points you made to make changes!
